question: A stakeholder requests a critical feature halfway through the sprint. The Product Owner agrees that it is important but believes changing the Sprint Backlog would jeopardize the Sprint Goal. What should happen?
optionA: The Developers should immediately replace lower-priority work with the new feature.
optionB: The Product Owner should add the feature to the Product Backlog and consider it during future backlog ordering unless the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.
optionC: The Scrum Master should cancel the sprint immediately.
optionD: The stakeholder should decide whether the sprint should continue.
explanation: Changes that threaten the Sprint Goal are generally deferred by placing them in the Product Backlog. A sprint should only be canceled if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.

question: Which metric is BEST suited for measuring how long it takes to complete a work item after development has started?
optionA: Velocity
optionB: Lead Time
optionC: Cycle Time
optionD: Cost Performance Index
explanation: Cycle Time measures the elapsed time from when work begins on an item until it is completed, making it useful for evaluating process efficiency.

question: A hybrid project manager wants to improve collaboration between predictive and Agile teams working on the same product. Which TWO actions would BEST support this objective? (Choose two.)
optionA: Establish regular synchronization meetings to review dependencies and shared milestones.
optionB: Create a common roadmap that aligns predictive deliverables with Agile releases.
optionC: Require each team to use completely independent schedules and reporting methods.
optionD: Restrict communication to formal change control meetings.
explanation: Hybrid projects benefit from coordinated planning, shared visibility and regular communication between predictive and Agile teams to manage dependencies and deliver value effectively.

question: A Scrum Team has successfully reduced defects through automated testing. Management now wants the team to maximize the speed of feature delivery by reducing testing activities. What should the Scrum Master recommend?
optionA: Reduce automated testing to increase development capacity.
optionB: Maintain appropriate quality practices because sustainable delivery depends on balancing speed and quality.
optionC: Perform testing only before major releases.
optionD: Move all testing responsibilities to a separate quality assurance team.
explanation: Agile emphasizes sustainable development and built-in quality. Reducing quality practices may increase short-term velocity but usually results in more defects, rework and lower long-term value.

question: Which Scrum event provides the BEST opportunity for the team to identify process improvements?
optionA: Sprint Review
optionB: Sprint Planning
optionC: Sprint Retrospective
optionD: Daily Scrum
explanation: The Sprint Retrospective is dedicated to inspecting how the team worked during the sprint and identifying actionable improvements for future sprints.

question: During Product Backlog Refinement, the Developers determine that a high-priority Product Backlog Item is too large to complete within a single sprint. What should happen NEXT?
optionA: Move the item to the bottom of the Product Backlog.
optionB: Split the Product Backlog Item into smaller, independently valuable items while preserving business value.
optionC: Increase the sprint length so the item can be completed.
optionD: Assign additional Developers exclusively to that Product Backlog Item.
explanation: Large backlog items should be decomposed into smaller, valuable increments that can be completed within a sprint, improving predictability and enabling earlier feedback.

question: Which Agile practice MOST directly supports maintaining a potentially releasable product increment at the end of every sprint?
optionA: Continuous Integration
optionB: Parametric Estimating
optionC: Critical Chain Scheduling
optionD: Resource Smoothing
explanation: Continuous Integration frequently merges and validates code changes, helping ensure that the product remains stable and potentially releasable throughout development.

question: A Scrum Team is experiencing increasing technical debt. Which TWO actions would BEST reduce future maintenance costs? (Choose two.)
optionA: Allocate capacity to refactor code while delivering new functionality.
optionB: Strengthen the Definition of Done to include appropriate quality practices.
optionC: Postpone all refactoring until the project has been completed.
optionD: Increase Work In Progress to accelerate feature development.
explanation: Managing technical debt requires continuous investment in code quality. Regular refactoring and a robust Definition of Done help prevent defects, reduce maintenance costs and improve long-term delivery performance.

question: A Scrum Team has delivered every Sprint Goal for the past six months, but stakeholders still believe progress is slow because they cannot see value until major releases. What should the Product Owner do?
optionA: Reduce the frequency of Sprint Reviews until larger features are completed.
optionB: Release valuable increments more frequently and communicate the business outcomes achieved after each release.
optionC: Increase sprint duration to include more functionality in every increment.
optionD: Require stakeholders to wait until the complete product has been finished.
explanation: Frequent releases and clear communication of business value improve stakeholder confidence and allow customers to realize benefits earlier.

question: Which role is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team?
optionA: Scrum Master
optionB: Project Sponsor
optionC: Product Owner
optionD: Development Manager
explanation: The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing product value through effective Product Backlog management and stakeholder engagement.

question: A hybrid project includes a predictive infrastructure component and an Agile software component. The predictive team completes its work months before the software is ready for integration. What should the project manager have done?
optionA: Delay infrastructure activities until software development is complete.
optionB: Develop an integrated roadmap that aligns deliverables and manages cross-team dependencies throughout the project.
optionC: Ask the Agile team to increase sprint length.
optionD: Allow each team to manage its own schedule independently.
explanation: Hybrid projects require integrated planning to synchronize predictive and Agile deliverables, reducing waiting time and dependency-related risks.

question: Which Agile concept encourages teams to deliver the smallest amount of functionality that provides measurable customer value?
optionA: Minimum Viable Product (MVP)
optionB: Work Breakdown Structure
optionC: Resource Leveling
optionD: Phase Gate Review
explanation: An MVP contains the minimum functionality needed to validate assumptions, obtain customer feedback and maximize learning with minimal investment.

question: A Scrum Team wants to improve forecasting accuracy for upcoming releases. Which TWO actions would BEST support this objective? (Choose two.)
optionA: Track historical velocity across multiple sprints.
optionB: Ensure Product Backlog Items are consistently refined before Sprint Planning.
optionC: Assign fixed story point values to all future Product Backlog Items before development begins.
optionD: Require Developers to estimate work in hours instead of relative size.
explanation: Reliable release forecasting depends on stable historical velocity and a well-refined Product Backlog. Relative estimation and ongoing refinement improve predictability more than fixed estimates.

question: A Scrum Team finishes every sprint with several low-priority defects that are deferred to future sprints. Over time, the backlog of defects continues to grow. What should the Scrum Master recommend?
optionA: Continue adding defects to the Product Backlog until the project is complete.
optionB: Work with the Product Owner and Developers to address technical debt and incorporate quality improvements into future sprints.
optionC: Create a separate defect resolution team to fix issues after each release.
optionD: Reduce the Definition of Done so more features can be completed.
explanation: Accumulating defects increase technical debt and future costs. The Scrum Team should continuously improve quality by addressing defects and strengthening engineering practices.

question: Which Agile estimation approach compares the relative size or complexity of Product Backlog Items rather than estimating duration?
optionA: Bottom-Up Estimating
optionB: Three-Point Estimating
optionC: Story Points
optionD: PERT Analysis
explanation: Story Points are used to estimate the relative effort, complexity and uncertainty of Product Backlog Items instead of predicting the exact amount of time required.

question: A stakeholder asks the Scrum Team to provide a detailed six-month feature commitment. The Product Owner expects priorities to change frequently during that period. What is the BEST response?
optionA: Commit to delivering all requested features within six months.
optionB: Provide a forecast based on current priorities while explaining that future Product Backlog ordering may change as new information becomes available.
optionC: Refuse to provide any forecast because Agile projects cannot estimate future work.
optionD: Ask the Scrum Master to create a detailed Gantt chart covering all future sprints.
explanation: Agile supports forecasting while acknowledging uncertainty. Forecasts should be based on current information and updated as priorities and knowledge evolve.

question: Which statement BEST describes the purpose of Continuous Delivery?
optionA: Every code change is automatically deployed directly to production.
optionB: Software is always in a releasable state, allowing releases whenever the business decides.
optionC: Developers deploy software only at the end of each release cycle.
optionD: Testing is postponed until all planned features have been completed.
explanation: Continuous Delivery ensures that software remains in a releasable state through automation and quality practices, while the decision to release remains a business choice.

question: A Scrum Team wants to improve stakeholder trust after several releases contained unexpected functionality. Which TWO actions would BEST help? (Choose two.)
optionA: Define clear acceptance criteria before implementation begins.
optionB: Validate completed functionality with stakeholders during Sprint Reviews.
optionC: Reduce stakeholder participation to avoid conflicting feedback.
optionD: Delay demonstrations until the complete product has been developed.
explanation: Clear acceptance criteria establish a shared understanding of expected behavior, while Sprint Reviews allow stakeholders to validate completed functionality and provide timely feedback, increasing transparency and trust.

question: A Scrum Team consistently meets its Sprint Goals, but the amount of unfinished work discovered during integration continues to increase. What should the Scrum Master recommend FIRST?
optionA: Increase the sprint duration to provide more time for integration.
optionB: Improve engineering practices by integrating work continuously throughout the sprint.
optionC: Move integration activities to the Sprint Review.
optionD: Reduce the number of Developers working on each Product Backlog Item.
explanation: Continuous Integration reduces integration risks by merging and validating changes frequently, allowing issues to be detected and resolved early instead of accumulating until the end of the sprint.

question: Which artifact provides a transparent view of all the work that might be needed to improve the product?
optionA: Sprint Backlog
optionB: Product Increment
optionC: Product Backlog
optionD: Release Plan
explanation: The Product Backlog is the single, ordered source of work for the Scrum Team and evolves continuously as the product and stakeholder needs change.

question: During a Sprint Review, stakeholders identify an unexpected market opportunity that could significantly increase product value. What should happen NEXT?
optionA: Immediately interrupt the sprint and begin developing the new feature.
optionB: The Product Owner should evaluate the opportunity and reorder the Product Backlog if appropriate.
optionC: The Scrum Master should decide whether the opportunity is worthwhile.
optionD: The Developers should implement the feature before completing the remaining backlog items.
explanation: The Sprint Review is intended to inspect the Increment and adapt the Product Backlog based on feedback, market conditions and new opportunities. The Product Owner is responsible for Product Backlog ordering.

question: Which Agile principle BEST supports reducing the cost of change throughout product development?
optionA: Deliver working software frequently and adapt based on feedback.
optionB: Complete detailed requirements before development begins.
optionC: Minimize stakeholder interaction after Sprint Planning.
optionD: Avoid modifying the Product Backlog after the first release.
explanation: Frequent delivery and continuous feedback enable teams to identify necessary changes early, when they are generally less expensive and easier to implement.

question: A hybrid project manager is preparing governance for an Agile delivery team while maintaining executive oversight. Which TWO approaches BEST balance agility with governance? (Choose two.)
optionA: Use lightweight governance with regular reviews based on product outcomes and risks.
optionB: Provide executives with transparent Agile metrics such as release forecasts and burnup charts.
optionC: Require formal approval before every Product Backlog reprioritization.
optionD: Measure team performance primarily by individual resource utilization.
explanation: Effective hybrid governance emphasizes transparency, value delivery and risk management while preserving the Agile team's ability to adapt quickly to changing priorities.

question: A Scrum Team consistently delivers high-quality increments, but the Product Owner finds that stakeholders rarely attend Sprint Reviews. What should the Scrum Master do FIRST?
optionA: Replace Sprint Reviews with email summaries.
optionB: Work with the Product Owner to understand stakeholder needs and improve the value and engagement of Sprint Reviews.
optionC: Require stakeholder attendance through executive management.
optionD: Cancel Sprint Reviews until stakeholders become available.
explanation: Sprint Reviews are collaborative working sessions. The Scrum Master should help improve stakeholder engagement by understanding expectations and ensuring the event delivers meaningful value.

question: What is the PRIMARY purpose of a Sprint Goal?
optionA: To define every task that Developers must complete.
optionB: To provide a single objective that gives the Scrum Team flexibility in implementing the selected work.
optionC: To establish the acceptance criteria for every Product Backlog Item.
optionD: To measure the team's productivity during the sprint.
explanation: The Sprint Goal provides a shared objective for the sprint while allowing Developers flexibility in how they accomplish the work needed to achieve that goal.

question: An Agile team is experiencing frequent production issues caused by inconsistent development environments. Which practice would MOST effectively address this problem?
optionA: Increase the length of each sprint.
optionB: Standardize environments through infrastructure automation and configuration management.
optionC: Delay deployments until the end of the release cycle.
optionD: Assign a separate team to manually verify every deployment.
explanation: Automated and standardized environments reduce configuration differences, improve deployment consistency and decrease production defects.

question: Which artifact is inspected during the Sprint Review to determine what has been accomplished during the sprint?
optionA: Sprint Backlog
optionB: Release Burndown Chart
optionC: Increment
optionD: Risk Register
explanation: The Sprint Review centers on inspecting the completed Increment and gathering stakeholder feedback to maximize future product value.

question: A Kanban team wants to improve throughput without sacrificing quality. Which TWO actions would BEST support this objective? (Choose two.)
optionA: Analyze workflow metrics to identify and eliminate bottlenecks.
optionB: Maintain appropriate Work In Progress limits and focus on finishing work before starting new items.
optionC: Increase Work In Progress limits whenever Developers become idle.
optionD: Measure success primarily by the number of tasks started each week.
explanation: Kanban improves throughput by optimizing flow. Identifying bottlenecks and limiting Work In Progress help teams complete work faster while maintaining quality.

question: A Scrum Team is consistently meeting its commitments, but customer feedback indicates that the delivered features are not solving the intended business problems. What should the Product Owner do FIRST?
optionA: Increase the number of Product Backlog Items selected each sprint.
optionB: Validate customer needs and desired outcomes before prioritizing additional work.
optionC: Ask the Scrum Master to improve team productivity.
optionD: Reduce the frequency of Sprint Reviews.
explanation: The Product Owner is responsible for maximizing value. Understanding customer outcomes before prioritizing future work ensures the team builds solutions that address real business needs.

question: Which Agile practice is primarily intended to reduce integration risks by merging code changes frequently?
optionA: Continuous Integration
optionB: Pair Programming
optionC: Story Mapping
optionD: Release Planning
explanation: Continuous Integration requires developers to integrate code changes frequently and automatically verify them, reducing integration issues and enabling rapid feedback.

question: A Product Owner notices that stakeholders frequently request features without explaining the underlying business problem. What is the BEST approach?
optionA: Implement the requests exactly as provided.
optionB: Collaborate with stakeholders to understand the desired outcomes before adding or prioritizing Product Backlog Items.
optionC: Reject all requests that lack detailed technical specifications.
optionD: Allow the Developers to determine which requests should be implemented.
explanation: Agile focuses on understanding customer problems and business outcomes rather than simply implementing requested features. This helps maximize value and avoid unnecessary work.

question: Which statement BEST describes the purpose of a burnup chart?
optionA: It shows the amount of work remaining in a sprint only.
optionB: It displays completed work against the total project scope, making scope changes visible.
optionC: It measures the number of defects discovered during testing.
optionD: It compares planned and actual project costs.
explanation: A burnup chart shows cumulative completed work relative to the total scope, allowing stakeholders to distinguish progress from scope changes.

question: A Scrum Team wants to shorten its release cycle while maintaining product quality. Which TWO actions would BEST support this objective? (Choose two.)
optionA: Increase deployment automation to reduce manual release activities.
optionB: Keep Product Backlog Items small enough to be completed within a sprint.
optionC: Postpone testing until the end of each release.
optionD: Increase Work In Progress to maximize resource utilization.
explanation: Deployment automation accelerates reliable releases, while small Product Backlog Items improve flow, reduce risk and enable frequent delivery without compromising quality.

question: A Scrum Team notices that the same impediment has affected the last four sprints. What should the Scrum Master do FIRST?
optionA: Ask the Product Owner to lower expectations for future sprints.
optionB: Facilitate the removal of the impediment by collaborating with the appropriate stakeholders and tracking progress.
optionC: Accept the impediment because the Sprint Goals are still being achieved.
optionD: Increase the sprint length to provide more time for the team.
explanation: Removing impediments is a key responsibility of the Scrum Master. Persistent impediments should be actively addressed by collaborating with stakeholders to eliminate their root causes.

question: Which Scrum accountability is responsible for coaching the organization in its Scrum adoption?
optionA: Product Owner
optionB: Project Sponsor
optionC: Scrum Master
optionD: Developers
explanation: The Scrum Master serves the Scrum Team and the organization by coaching Scrum adoption, facilitating Scrum events and helping remove impediments.

question: A Product Owner wants to accelerate learning about a risky new feature before committing significant development effort. Which approach is MOST appropriate?
optionA: Develop the complete feature before requesting customer feedback.
optionB: Create a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) to validate assumptions with real users.
optionC: Increase the sprint duration to include more functionality.
optionD: Perform detailed predictive planning for the entire feature set.
explanation: An MVP enables rapid validation of assumptions with minimal investment, allowing the Product Owner to make evidence-based decisions before committing additional resources.

question: What is the PRIMARY benefit of conducting Product Backlog Refinement on a regular basis?
optionA: It replaces Sprint Planning.
optionB: It improves the clarity, size and priority of Product Backlog Items before they are selected for a sprint.
optionC: It eliminates the need for Sprint Reviews.
optionD: It guarantees a fixed project schedule.
explanation: Regular Product Backlog Refinement helps ensure that high-priority items are well understood, appropriately sized and ready for consideration during Sprint Planning.

question: A Scrum Team wants to improve the predictability of its sprint forecasts. Which TWO actions would BEST help achieve this objective? (Choose two.)
optionA: Select work based on the team's historical velocity and current capacity.
optionB: Ensure Product Backlog Items meet the team's Definition of Ready before Sprint Planning.
optionC: Require Developers to work overtime whenever forecasts are missed.
optionD: Increase the number of Product Backlog Items selected to maximize utilization.
explanation: Using historical velocity together with current team capacity improves forecasting accuracy. Well-refined Product Backlog Items that satisfy the team's Definition of Ready also reduce uncertainty during Sprint Planning.

question: A Scrum Team has noticed that its velocity has remained stable for several sprints, but the release date forecast continues to change because new Product Backlog Items are frequently added. What should the Product Owner do?
optionA: Prevent stakeholders from submitting new Product Backlog Items.
optionB: Continuously reorder the Product Backlog while communicating how scope changes affect release forecasts.
optionC: Increase the team's velocity target to maintain the original release date.
optionD: Commit to a fixed scope regardless of changing business priorities.
explanation: Velocity supports forecasting, but release dates are also affected by scope changes. The Product Owner should manage stakeholder expectations by explaining the impact of backlog changes on delivery forecasts.

question: Which artifact contains the Product Goal and an ordered list of everything known to be needed in the product?
optionA: Sprint Backlog
optionB: Increment
optionC: Product Backlog
optionD: Release Roadmap
explanation: The Product Backlog is an evolving, ordered list of work needed for the product and includes the Product Goal that provides long-term direction.

question: A Scrum Team frequently waits several days for code reviews before work can be completed. What should the Scrum Master recommend FIRST?
optionA: Increase the Work In Progress limit.
optionB: Identify the bottleneck and collaborate with the team to improve workflow, such as through peer reviews or pair programming.
optionC: Move all code reviews to the end of the sprint.
optionD: Assign code reviews exclusively to the most experienced Developer.
explanation: Agile teams continuously improve flow by identifying bottlenecks and implementing collaborative practices that reduce delays while maintaining quality.

question: Which statement BEST describes servant leadership in an Agile environment?
optionA: The leader assigns work based on individual performance rankings.
optionB: The leader focuses on enabling the team to succeed by removing obstacles and supporting continuous improvement.
optionC: The leader approves every technical decision before implementation.
optionD: The leader measures success primarily by resource utilization.
explanation: Servant leaders support, coach and empower teams by removing impediments, fostering collaboration and creating an environment where teams can continuously improve.

question: A Product Owner wants to ensure that future Product Backlog Items deliver measurable business value. Which TWO actions would BEST support this objective? (Choose two.)
optionA: Define measurable business outcomes or success criteria for high-priority Product Backlog Items.
optionB: Validate completed features using customer feedback and product usage metrics.
optionC: Prioritize Product Backlog Items based primarily on the amount of development effort required.
optionD: Avoid changing Product Backlog priorities after Sprint Planning.
explanation: Measurable outcomes and continuous validation with customers help ensure that Product Backlog Items contribute to real business value and support evidence-based decision making.

question: A Scrum Team consistently completes Sprint Goals, but each release requires several weeks of manual regression testing before deployment. What should the Scrum Master recommend?
optionA: Increase the sprint duration so more regression testing can be completed.
optionB: Invest in automated regression testing to reduce release delays and improve delivery frequency.
optionC: Perform regression testing only after major releases.
optionD: Reduce the Definition of Done to exclude regression testing.
explanation: Automated regression testing shortens release cycles, improves quality and supports frequent, reliable product releases without increasing manual effort.

question: Which Scrum event is primarily focused on planning the work needed to achieve the Sprint Goal?
optionA: Sprint Review
optionB: Sprint Retrospective
optionC: Sprint Planning
optionD: Daily Scrum
explanation: Sprint Planning establishes the Sprint Goal, selects Product Backlog Items and creates the initial Sprint Backlog needed to achieve the sprint objective.

question: A Product Owner discovers that a competitor has launched a feature similar to one currently under development. What should the Product Owner do FIRST?
optionA: Continue development exactly as originally planned.
optionB: Assess the impact on product strategy and reorder the Product Backlog based on the new market information.
optionC: Cancel the current sprint immediately.
optionD: Ask the Developers to implement additional features without consulting stakeholders.
explanation: Agile teams respond to changing market conditions. The Product Owner should evaluate the competitive impact and adapt Product Backlog priorities to maximize business value.

question: Which metric measures the average number of work items completed during a specific period in a flow-based system?
optionA: Velocity
optionB: Throughput
optionC: Lead Time
optionD: Schedule Performance Index
explanation: Throughput measures how many work items are completed over a given period and is commonly used in Kanban and other flow-based Agile approaches.

question: A Scrum Team wants to improve product quality while maintaining a sustainable pace. Which TWO actions would BEST support this objective? (Choose two.)
optionA: Include code reviews and automated testing as part of the Definition of Done.
optionB: Refactor code regularly to reduce technical debt.
optionC: Delay quality improvements until after the planned release.
optionD: Measure success primarily by the number of Product Backlog Items completed.
explanation: Embedding quality practices in the Definition of Done and continuously reducing technical debt improve long-term maintainability while supporting sustainable product delivery.

question: A Scrum Team consistently delivers valuable increments, but the Product Owner struggles to determine which features provide the greatest business value after release. What should the Product Owner do?
optionA: Prioritize features based only on development effort.
optionB: Define measurable success metrics before implementation and evaluate them after each release.
optionC: Ask stakeholders to rank completed features after every sprint without collecting usage data.
optionD: Increase the number of Product Backlog Items delivered in each sprint.
explanation: Agile product management relies on evidence-based decisions. Defining measurable outcomes before implementation allows the Product Owner to assess whether delivered features actually create business value.

question: Which Agile artifact or tool is MOST commonly used to visualize the flow of work through different stages?
optionA: Risk Register
optionB: Kanban Board
optionC: Responsibility Assignment Matrix
optionD: Network Diagram
explanation: A Kanban Board visualizes workflow, making work items, bottlenecks and Work In Progress visible so teams can improve flow.

question: A Scrum Team completes development early but repeatedly discovers defects during final testing at the end of the sprint. Which improvement would MOST likely address this issue?
optionA: Increase the number of Product Backlog Items selected each sprint.
optionB: Adopt Test-Driven Development (TDD) or similar practices that build quality into development.
optionC: Move all testing activities to the Sprint Review.
optionD: Reduce stakeholder involvement until after release.
explanation: Practices such as Test-Driven Development improve code quality by identifying defects earlier, reducing rework and supporting potentially releasable increments.

question: In Scrum, who is responsible for deciding how the selected Product Backlog Items will be accomplished during the sprint?
optionA: Product Owner
optionB: Project Sponsor
optionC: Developers
optionD: Scrum Master
explanation: The Developers are responsible for creating the Sprint Backlog and determining how the selected Product Backlog Items will be implemented to achieve the Sprint Goal.

question: An Agile organization wants to improve transparency across multiple Scrum Teams working on the same product. Which TWO actions would BEST support this objective? (Choose two.)
optionA: Use shared information radiators that display progress, dependencies and release status.
optionB: Hold regular cross-team synchronization meetings to identify and resolve dependencies.
optionC: Allow each Scrum Team to maintain independent definitions of product completion.
optionD: Limit communication between Scrum Teams to Sprint Reviews only.
explanation: Shared information radiators and regular cross-team synchronization improve transparency, expose dependencies early and help multiple Scrum Teams coordinate effectively toward common product goals.

question: A Scrum Team consistently delivers working software, but customer feedback reveals that many users struggle to use new features. What should the Product Owner do FIRST?
optionA: Increase the number of training sessions after each release.
optionB: Gather additional customer insights to understand usability issues and reprioritize the Product Backlog accordingly.
optionC: Reduce the number of features delivered in each sprint.
optionD: Ask the Scrum Master to improve the Daily Scrum.
explanation: The Product Owner should use customer feedback to understand the root cause of usability issues and adapt Product Backlog priorities to maximize user value.

question: Which Agile practice encourages two Developers to work together on the same piece of code to improve quality and knowledge sharing?
optionA: Pair Programming
optionB: Story Mapping
optionC: Affinity Estimating
optionD: Value Stream Mapping
explanation: Pair Programming is an Extreme Programming (XP) practice where two Developers collaborate on the same code, improving quality, reducing defects and increasing knowledge sharing.

question: A Scrum Team frequently delays technical improvements because stakeholders always prioritize new features. Over time, delivery speed has begun to decline. What should the Product Owner do?
optionA: Continue prioritizing only customer-facing features.
optionB: Balance business features with technical improvements that sustain long-term product value.
optionC: Assign technical improvements to a separate maintenance team.
optionD: Increase sprint duration to accommodate additional work.
explanation: Technical improvements reduce technical debt and improve future delivery capability. The Product Owner should balance immediate business value with long-term product sustainability.

question: Which Agile concept focuses on optimizing the entire system rather than maximizing the efficiency of individual resources?
optionA: Resource Utilization
optionB: Systems Thinking
optionC: Fast Tracking
optionD: Critical Path Method
explanation: Systems Thinking encourages teams to optimize end-to-end value delivery rather than improving isolated activities that may create bottlenecks elsewhere in the system.

question: A Scrum Team is preparing for a major product release involving several external vendors. Which TWO actions would BEST reduce integration risk? (Choose two.)
optionA: Integrate vendor deliverables frequently throughout development rather than waiting until the release date.
optionB: Establish regular communication with vendors to review dependencies, interfaces and delivery progress.
optionC: Delay integration until every vendor has completed all planned work.
optionD: Accept vendor deliverables without verification to maintain the release schedule.
explanation: Frequent integration and regular coordination with vendors expose interface issues early, reduce dependency risks and improve the likelihood of a successful release.

question: A Scrum Team has improved its velocity over the last several sprints, but customer satisfaction has not increased. Which metric should the Product Owner focus on NEXT?
optionA: The number of story points completed per sprint.
optionB: Business outcomes and customer adoption of delivered features.
optionC: The number of hours worked by the Developers.
optionD: The percentage of Product Backlog Items completed on schedule.
explanation: Velocity measures output, not value. The Product Owner should evaluate business outcomes, customer adoption and satisfaction to determine whether the product is delivering meaningful value.

question: What is the PRIMARY objective of a Daily Scrum?
optionA: Provide a project status update to stakeholders.
optionB: Inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the plan for the next 24 hours.
optionC: Review completed Product Backlog Items with the Product Owner.
optionD: Assign new work to individual Developers.
explanation: The Daily Scrum is a planning event for the Developers to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adjust their plan to maximize the likelihood of achieving it.

question: During a Sprint Review, stakeholders request several enhancements that would significantly increase the scope of an existing feature. What should the Product Owner do?
optionA: Add the requested enhancements directly to the current Sprint Backlog.
optionB: Evaluate the requested enhancements and reorder the Product Backlog based on expected value and strategic priorities.
optionC: Reject the requests because the feature has already been completed.
optionD: Ask the Scrum Master to determine whether the enhancements should be implemented.
explanation: The Product Owner evaluates stakeholder feedback and orders the Product Backlog according to value, risk and product strategy. New requests should be considered during backlog management rather than inserted into an active sprint.

question: Which Agile concept emphasizes delaying irreversible decisions until the latest responsible moment while enough information is available?
optionA: Rolling Wave Planning
optionB: Last Responsible Moment
optionC: Critical Chain
optionD: Scope Baseline
explanation: The Last Responsible Moment is a Lean and Agile principle that encourages delaying irreversible decisions until sufficient knowledge exists without unnecessarily delaying delivery.

question: A Scrum Team wants to improve the effectiveness of its Sprint Retrospectives. Which TWO actions would BEST support continuous improvement? (Choose two.)
optionA: Identify one or two realistic improvement actions and implement them during the next sprint.
optionB: Use objective team metrics and observations to analyze root causes rather than assigning blame.
optionC: Focus the discussion primarily on individual performance ratings.
optionD: Avoid discussing recurring issues to keep the meeting positive.
explanation: Effective Sprint Retrospectives produce actionable improvements and use objective evidence to identify root causes. Continuous improvement depends on experimentation, learning and psychological safety rather than blame.

question: A Scrum Team consistently finishes development before the end of the sprint, but deployment to production takes several weeks because of a manual approval process. What should the Scrum Master recommend FIRST?
optionA: Increase the sprint duration to match the deployment schedule.
optionB: Collaborate with the organization to streamline the deployment process while maintaining appropriate governance.
optionC: Reduce the number of Product Backlog Items selected each sprint.
optionD: Delay Sprint Reviews until deployment has been completed.
explanation: The Scrum Master serves the organization by helping remove systemic impediments. Streamlining deployment while preserving governance improves flow and enables faster value delivery.

question: Which Agile planning artifact provides a high-level view of expected product evolution over time without committing to detailed scope?
optionA: Work Breakdown Structure
optionB: Product Roadmap
optionC: Issue Log
optionD: Procurement Management Plan
explanation: A Product Roadmap communicates the intended direction of the product over time while allowing flexibility to adapt as priorities and market conditions evolve.

question: During Sprint Planning, the Developers estimate that the highest-priority Product Backlog Item cannot be completed because of technical uncertainty. What should the Scrum Team do?
optionA: Commit to the item and extend the sprint if necessary.
optionB: Work with the Product Owner to split the item or create a time-boxed Spike to reduce uncertainty.
optionC: Remove the item permanently from the Product Backlog.
optionD: Assign the item to the most experienced Developer without changing the plan.
explanation: When significant uncertainty exists, the Scrum Team should collaborate with the Product Owner to reduce risk by splitting the work or using a Spike before committing to full implementation.

question: Which Lean principle encourages completing work before starting additional work in order to improve overall flow?
optionA: Maximize Work In Progress
optionB: Optimize Local Efficiency
optionC: Limit Work in Progress
optionD: Increase Batch Size
explanation: Limiting Work in Progress improves flow, reduces context switching, exposes bottlenecks and enables faster delivery of completed work.

question: A Product Owner wants to improve evidence-based decision making after each release. Which TWO actions would BEST support this objective? (Choose two.)
optionA: Define measurable Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for new features before implementation.
optionB: Analyze customer behavior and product usage data after each release.
optionC: Prioritize future Product Backlog Items based only on stakeholder opinions.
optionD: Measure team success exclusively by the number of story points completed.
explanation: Evidence-based product management relies on defining measurable success criteria and validating them using real customer and product data. This enables informed Product Backlog decisions focused on maximizing business value.
